messages:
Jordan: Dropping a quick mock for the micro-metrics chart in the console. Two quick asks: how to surface extreme values without wrecking scale, and what the default legend layout should be in the compact panel?

Mina: For scale, show an overflow indicator (small up-arrow) on points beyond the 97th percentile and a dashed clamp line at the boundary. Clicking it toggles expanded axis. Tooltip copy: 'Values above 97th percentile collapsed for readability. Show full range.'

Toby: Legend: condensed by default for small panels (swatch + short name). Add a small badge for overflow count like '+4' and make the badge interactive to expand. Keyboard: legend items must be focusable and togglable with Enter/Space.

A11y-Lead: Add an offscreen live region that announces when the chart is clipped: 'Chart clipped at 97th percentile, 4 points hidden.' Careful with the word 'hidden' vs 'collapsed' — 'collapsed' is less alarming. Also ensure overflow badge has >=4.5:1 contrast.

Mina: Units: use short SI suffixes on ticks (ms / s). Auto-switch: ms if <1000, s otherwise. For screen readers, include full units in the aria-label like 'Latency in milliseconds (ms)'.

Jordan: Smoothing defaults: OFF. Offer presets: None / rolling mean 1m / median 5m. When smoothing is on show a tiny label on the legend 'smoothed' with hover text explaining the method. Also include a clear 'view raw' button.

Toby: Visual cue idea: dim clipped points and show a tiny caret glyph at the plot edge for each series with clipped values. For exports (PNG/SVG) expand by default so reports don't drop data.

Design-Bot: Linked checklist: https://redwood.internal/ux/compact-chart-guidelines.

Jordan: I'll update the figma with condensed legend, overflow badge, dashed clamp line and ARIA copy. Will circle back for a11y pass tomorrow.

A11y-Lead: Thanks — I'll test with NVDA/VoiceOver and report focus/readout issues.

Toby: :thumbsup:
